## ability-resolutions-this-turn

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a per-turn, per-ability resolution counter the DSL can read, e.g. {"resolutions_this_turn": "self"} evaluating to how many times *this printed triggered ability* has already resolved this turn (counting the resolution in progress), reset in the turn ledger alongside `spells_cast` and `creatures_died`. Wanted here as the condition of an `if`: {"cmp": {"left": {"resolutions_this_turn": "self"}, "op": "==", "right": {"const": 2}}}, whose `then` branch is {"op": "add_counters", "counter": "+1/+1", "amount": {"counters_on": {"counter": "+1/+1", "objects": {"target": true}}}, "objects": {"target": true}} and whose `else` branch adds one counter
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Everything else on this card is already sayable: the trigger is `permanent_enters` filtered to Lands you control, the doubling is `add_counters` with an amount of `counters_on` the target, and `if` already has `then`/`else` so the printed "instead" needs no replacement machinery. The only unsayable part is the count. `value_keys` reaches the turn ledger for spells cast, creatures died, cards drawn, damage taken, life lost and cards to graveyard, but nothing counts ability resolutions -- and there is no lands-entered-this-turn value to stand in for it either (which would be wrong anyway: the printed text counts resolutions of the ability, not land drops, so a countered or fizzled trigger must not advance it). `set_flag`/`has_flag` is the nearest recording mechanism and it is the wrong shape twice over: it is explicitly one-way (`op_set_flag` only adds to `obj.flags`, there is no clear_flag op and nothing empties `flags` at end of turn), so a flag written on the first landfall would still be set on every later turn and would make the *third* and every subsequent resolution double as well, instead of only the second. Faking the reset with an extra end-step ability that erases the mark is also barred: it implements no printed sentence, so the residual gate rejects the card.

## look-at-hand

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** An effect op that shows the cards in a targeted player's hand privately to the ability's controller only, leaving them hidden from everyone else and leaving them in hand -- e.g. `{"op": "look_at_hand", "player": {"target": ...}}`
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `reveal` is the closest op in `ops`, but revealing is public information shown to all players, which is a strictly different game action from looking; a card that reveals an opponent's hand tells the opponent's opponents things Glasses of Urza does not. `reveal` also takes an `objects` selector over cards and has no `player` argument, so it cannot be pointed at a hand at all.

## look-at-top-n

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** an effect that bounds a pool to the top N cards of a library and then lets the chooser take any number of the cards in that pool that match a selector to a named destination, leaving the rest where they were. Wanted here as something like {"op": "look_at_top", "amount": {"const": 20}, "selector": {"types": ["Land"]}, "count": "any", "destination": "battlefield", "tapped": true, "shuffle": true}. The free-subset decision this needs already exists -- `scry` and `surveil` both call `ask_objects(..., 0, len(top), ...)` over `library[:amount]` -- so the missing piece is a top-N pool whose destination is not fixed to the bottom of the library or the graveyard.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `search_library` is the only op that moves library cards to the battlefield tapped, and it builds its pool from the *entire* library (`for oid in ctx.state.players[pid].library`), with no amount/depth clause. Written with it, this card would be an unconditional tutor for every land in a 40+ card deck rather than a look at twenty, which is a strictly stronger card and not the printed line -- the difference is exactly what makes the card a gamble. The three ops that do read `library[:amount]` -- `scry`, `surveil`, `two_piles` -- each hard-wire where the looked-at cards may go (bottom of library, graveyard, hand-or-graveyard); none accepts a destination or a selector, so none can put lands onto the battlefield tapped. The selector language cannot close the gap either: `resolve_pool` maps `zone: "library"` to the whole `zone_list(Zone.LIBRARY)`, and `SELECTOR_KEYS` has no depth/top-of-library key, so `put_onto_battlefield` over a library selector would also see every card in the deck. Also note `count` in a selector is "all" or a fixed number, so the printed "any number" needs the free-subset spelling tracked under `any_number_of` unless this op bakes it in the way `scry` and `surveil` do.

## search-library-and-graveyard

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a search whose pool is the union of two of your own zones -- your library and your graveyard -- from which one card total is chosen and moved. Wanted here as {"op": "search_zones", "player": "you", "zones": ["library", "graveyard"], "count": 1, "destination": "battlefield", "selector": {"types": ["Creature"], "mana_value": {"op": "<=", "value": {"x": true}}}}. The count is over the combined pool, so finding in one zone must exclude finding in the other.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `search_library` builds its pool from `ctx.state.players[pid].library` alone, and `return_from_graveyard` defaults its selector to `zone: graveyard`; running both in sequence is a different card, because each takes its own count and Finale would fetch up to two creatures instead of one. The selector language cannot merge the zones either: `resolve_pool` reads a single `zone` key and `validate_selector` explicitly rejects `zone` inside an `any_of` branch ("put 'zone' on the outer selector; a branch filters the pool it already chose"), so `any_of` unions descriptions, never zones. A `choose_mode` over a library mode and a graveyard mode gets the count right but is still not the printed line: "and/or" lets the player look through both zones before committing, while a mode choice is made blind and locks out the other zone.
- **(decision)** a way to make the shuffle conditional on whether the library was actually looked at during this resolution -- either an automatic part of the union-search op (shuffle iff the library half of the pool was examined) or a condition key that reads the choice the search just made
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `search_library` shuffles unconditionally unless `"shuffle": false` is set at authoring time, and the `shuffle` op is likewise static. `condition_keys` can ask about flags (`has_flag`, via `set_flag`), zones and comparisons, but nothing observes which zone a search decision touched, and `set_flag` cannot be attached to one branch of a choice the engine makes inside a single op.
